title: Bayleaf Financial - Activation Sprint Launch
summary: Kickoff for Bayleaf's activation sprint. Confirmed pilot scope (customer support triage assistant), network/VPC requirements, basic security guardrails (KMS + audit logs), staging tenant provisioning timeline, and next steps: security package, SSO config, and a technical deep-dive to baseline latency/cost expectations.
next_steps: Jordan to send SOC 2 + security packet by 2025-05-30
Priya to schedule technical deep-dive (latency & batch config) w/ Lina and Marcus week of 6/2
Provision staging tenant and share creds (Redwood CSM to confirm) by 6/4
action_items: Jordan Kim - send security packet, SOC2 report, and link to runbook (due: 2025-05-30)
Priya Shah - schedule benchmark deep-dive and request sample payloads (due: 2025-06-02)
Marcus Reed - share VPC CIDR, firewall rules, and expected egress IPs for peering (due: 2025-06-03)
Evelyn Cho - confirm data residency & retention policy for pilot (due: 2025-06-04)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-29
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ana (Redwood CSM), Marcus, Lina, Sanjay, Evelyn (Bayleaf)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for being here. this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. great to meet you all. quick round robin?
[00:10] Marcus: Marcus Reed here, head of data at Bayleaf. we'll be the primary contact for the pilot.
[00:15] Lina: Lina Park, platform eng. I'll handle the VPC peering and infra work.
[00:20] Sanjay: Sanjay Iyer, CTO. Mostly here to watch the SLOs and timelines.
[00:25] Evelyn: Evelyn Cho, security, i'll review the compliance bits.
[00:30] Jordan: Awesome. Ok quick agenda: confirm pilot scope, network and security intake, staging tenant timing, and next steps. Ana will own provisioning and enablement details.
[00:45] Ana: Hi all. we'll provision a staging tenant first, default quotas, can adjust later. Expect a link once we finalize the CIDR.
[00:55] Marcus: Great. Pilot scope — we talked about a customer-support triage assistant, ingesting chat logs and returning recommended article links and severity score. Expected peak QPS is about 15, average payload size ~1.2k tokens.
[01:12] Priya: Ok that's helpful. For latency targets are you aiming for sub-300ms per token or overall response under 1s? sometimes the per-token is noisy.
[01:20] Marcus: Prefer overall response under 1.2s for typical 20-token replies. Cost is also a concern, so we might trade a bit of latency for lower unit cost.
[01:30] Priya: Noted. We'll propose batching and prefix caching; Redwood's KV cache helps with repeated session context — sometimes transcribed as K V cash in past notes.
[01:42] Lina: On networking, we prefer VPC peering with strict egress ranges. we'll provide CIDR and a list of allowed ports.
[01:50] Ana: we'll need the CIDR and a contact for peering. Once we receive that we'll open the staging tenant and coordinate a quick cert exchange.
[02:05] Evelyn: Security-wise: SOC 2, SAML SSO, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys are must-haves. can you share your SOC 2 report? also audit log retention min 90 days.
[02:20] Jordan: absolutely. i'll send SOC 2 and our public security packet after this call. we support KMS/HSM integrations; for pilot we can use Redwood-managed keys but we can schedule KMS in the next phase.
[02:35] Sanjay: For data residency — we need logs stored in us-east-1 only. is that doable in your hosted flow?
[02:42] Priya: Yes, we can pin region to us-east-1 for the tenant. For private deployments we can also do VPC-only but that comes with more lead time.
[02:55] Marcus: Team also asked about model variants and rollback. If you do an A/B we need deterministic sampling for experiments.
[03:03] Priya: Redwoods platform supports canary rollouts and a model catalog, you can pin a model version and we have automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants if capacity is constrained. sorry if product name came out odd in notes before — sometimes 'Redwood Private' looks like 'Redwood Privet' in auto text.
[03:22] Lina: Great. On IAM — we use okta SAML. we need to map roles to Bayleaf groups.
[03:30] Ana: We'll send the SAML metadata and an enablement doc. mapping is straightforward with group-to-role templates.
[03:40] Marcus: On benchmarking — we want a baseline: p95 latency for 20- token response, cost per 1k tokens, and memory/kv cache hit rates. can you run a small benchmark with our sample payloads?
[03:55] Priya: yes. priya: i'll own the bench. we'll need sample payloads and expected concurrency patterns. i'll plan a 1-hour run and share results.
[04:05] Marcus: i'll share a small dataset and an anonymized chat sample after this call.
[04:12] Jordan: timeline wise: we aim to be live with the pilot in three weeks. week 1: staging tenant + security signoff, week 2: benchmarking and initial model config, week 3: pilot run and collect metrics. does that timeline sound feasible?
[04:28] Sanjay: three weeks is aggressive but doable if we get network and security docs quickly.
[04:35] Evelyn: i can review SOC2 and reply within 48 hours if Jordan sends it today.
[04:42] Ana: provisioning wise we'll need 48-72 hours after we receive CIDR and SAML metadata.
[04:50] Jordan: ok, recap of owners: Jordan — security packet and runbook. Priya — bench deep-dive session w/ Marcus & Lina. Ana — staging tenant provisioning. Marcus/Evelyn — provide CIDR, sample payloads, and residency confirmation.
[05:05] Marcus: quick question — cost controls. do you have per-route budgets or token caps?
[05:12] Priya: yes, we can set per-route quotas and token limits, plus alerting. Redwood Optimize will also suggest batching and quantization profiles for cost savings.
[05:28] Sanjay: on compliance: we will want to review contract terms about data deletion after pilot end.
[05:33] Jordan: we have data retention controls and can set auto-delete windows; legal will follow up if needed.
[05:40] Lina: any docs or runbooks to share now?
[05:44] Ana: I'll drop a link to the onboarding runbook, network checklist, and SAML template in the follow-up email.
[05:53] Evelyn: one more: audit logs export format? we prefer json with timestamps in UTC.
[06:00] Priya: we can export logs in JSON. retention, indexing, and S3 export can be configured.
[06:08] Jordan: great. Are there any blockers we haven't addressed?
[06:12] Marcus: none from my side. main blocker is the VPC CIDR and firewall rules.
[06:18] Lina: i'll prioritize that today and share with Jordan & Ana.
[06:22] Ana: i'll put the tenant provisioning ticket in motion as soon as we have CIDR.
[06:26] Jordan: ok final recap and next steps — same as action items. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench deep-dive and a 30-minute SSO walkthrough.
[06:38] Sanjay: thanks all. excited to get started.
[06:42] Jordan: thanks everyone, i'll send the security packet now and follow up with the runbook links. talk soon.
[06:48] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hear - 'KV cache' noted as 'K V cash' and 'Redwood Private' sometimes 'Redwood Privet'. natural filler words and some speaker overlaps.
